title: EDRi Annual Report 2025: Championing digital rights in the deregulation era
summary: European Digital Rights' self-published Annual Report 2025 — an organizational retrospective, surfaced by the Scanner as a Privacy candidate.
body: Editor's note. The candidate URL was live and real (HTTP 200, datePublished 29 June 2026) — this is not a hallucinated link. The problem is that it resolves to EDRi's own Annual Report 2025, filed under the 'Annual reports' section of edri.org: an advocacy organization summarizing its own year of work under a promotional frame. An annual report is a yearly self-summary, not a discrete news event. There is nothing for a wire service to have independently covered, and no third-party-verifiable claim to grade — the subject is the source, so it can never clear our 2-independent-sources floor. We like EDRi's work; we cannot run 'org publishes report about org' as reporting. Killed by the Source Checker at Pass 1 (confidence 0.20) under the self-summary/roundup auto-kill pattern. EIC ratified. If the report surfaces a specific concrete development — a named ruling, an EU legislative milestone, a campaign outcome — the Scanner can pull that as its own candidate with a real lead, and we'll grade it on its own sourcing.
rejection_reason: self-summary/roundup auto-kill | EDRi Annual Report 2025 is an org's own yearly retrospective — no discrete news event, inherently single-source (subject = source), below the 0.5 threshold
